primary_citation.popular_name: Authentication Required Before Admission — the procedural gate that bars all unauthenticated writings from evidence

structural_location.chapter: CHAPTER 1. Authentication and Proof of Writings [1400 - 1454]
structural_location.section_history: Enacted by Stats. 1965, Ch. 299. NEVER AMENDED — the section is in its original 1965 form.

verbatim_text.verbatim_full: (a) Authentication of a writing is required before it may be received in evidence. (b) Authentication of a writing is required before secondary evidence of its content may be received in evidence.

structural_breakdown.subsection_a: (a) Authentication of a writing is required before it may be received in evidence — this is the primary gate. No writing enters evidence without first being authenticated under § 1400.
structural_breakdown.subsection_b: (b) Authentication of a writing is required before secondary evidence of its content may be received in evidence — this closes the secondary-evidence loophole. Even if the original writing is unavailable, and secondary evidence (copies, testimony about contents) is offered under the secondary evidence rule, authentication is still required.
structural_breakdown.doctrinal_significance: § 1401 is the enforcement mechanism for § 1400. Where § 1400 defines what authentication means, § 1401 makes authentication mandatory. Together they create a two-part gate: definition (§ 1400) + requirement (§ 1401). A party who offers a writing without authenticating it has offered nothing the court can receive.

amendment_history.event: Original enactment as part of the 1965 Evidence Code recodification.

amendment_history_note: § 1401 has NEVER been amended since its 1965 enactment. The text is in its original form.

steward_case_relevance_audit.purpose: § 1401 is the procedural lever that makes authentication mandatory. In the steward's case, multiple writings were relied on in proceedings without evidence that they were ever properly authenticated: unsigned custody evaluation reports, disputed police reports, medical records with gaps, and financial documents in the house sale. § 1401 is the rule that says those writings could not have been received in evidence without authentication — and if they were, the admission was improper.

factor_audits.what_the_statute_requires: Authentication is required before a writing may be received in evidence. Period. No exceptions within this section.
factor_audits.what_the_record_shows: Unsigned reports submitted in family law proceedings, a police report that does not exist in the issuing agency's records system (per OPD October 2025 records pickup), and 19 unsigned documents in the Honeysuckle house sale — all appear to have been relied upon without authentication foundation.
factor_audits.audit_status: CRITICAL — every contested writing in the steward's case must pass through this gate.

factor_audits.what_the_statute_requires: Even secondary evidence of a writing's content requires authentication. A party cannot avoid the authentication requirement by offering a copy, summary, or oral testimony about the writing's contents instead of the original.
factor_audits.what_the_record_shows: Where originals have been lost, destroyed, or are in the possession of opposing parties, secondary evidence may be offered — but only after the secondary evidence itself is authenticated. This closes the door on offering photocopies of unauthenticated originals.
factor_audits.audit_status: RELEVANT — secondary evidence of contested documents still requires authentication.

steward_case_relevance_audit.audit_summary: § 1401 is the mandatory gate. Combined with § 1400's definition, it means: if a writing was received in evidence without authentication, the admission was error. The steward's case file contains multiple writings that appear to have been received without this gate being satisfied.

owner_citizen.ownership_note: § 1401 is the enforcement arm of the authentication requirement. Structurally inseparable from § 1400.
